title: SecurePay Guard
tagline: Every day Nigerians lose money to hidden mobile‑money scams
whyNow: Cyber‑fraud arrests have spiked – 1,462 suspects were just detained in a continent‑wide crackdown and AI‑driven scams are doubling worldwide, making real‑time protection urgent.

proof.text: 1,462 suspects arrested for yahoo‑yahoo and cyber fraud across African countries
Mobile money scammers keep hiding in plain sight, exploiting users of mobile money services
AI‑driven digital deception is surging, with online scams doubling globally

marketGap: Consumers have no real‑time, user‑facing alerts or insurance for suspicious mobile‑money transactions; existing bank‑level fraud tools are opaque and do not reimburse victims.
executionPlan: Build an MVP mobile app that plugs into the APIs of major mobile‑money operators to monitor transactions in real time using AI‑driven risk scoring. Launch a beta in Nigeria with a limited set of high‑risk transaction types, partner with a micro‑insurer to offer instant reimbursement for confirmed fraud, and charge a small fee per protected transaction or a subscription for premium alerts.
competitor: None offers a consumer‑level, real‑time fraud‑alert and instant reimbursement service for mobile money – the closest is internal bank fraud detection, which is not accessible to end‑users.
trend: Rising AI‑driven scams and exploding mobile‑money adoption across Africa make instant fraud protection a timely necessity.

title: FeeGuard: Transparent School Fee Platform
tagline: Parents are hit with hidden extra school fees and unpredictable hikes.
whyNow: Recent reports of extra fees and soaring tuition across Nigeria, alongside legislative attempts to curb fee hikes, create urgent demand for a tool that guarantees fee transparency and protects family budgets.

proof.text: Parents report being charged extra school fees despite government restrictions.
Parents in Kogi describe education as a luxury due to rising school fees.
Legislators are seeking to suspend fee increases at tertiary institutions.

marketGap: No existing private platform offers real‑time, blockchain‑backed fee breakdowns and escrowed payments for schools, leaving parents exposed to hidden and sudden fee hikes.
executionPlan: Develop an MVP mobile app that integrates with schools' fee management systems to publish standardized fee structures and lock tuition payments in a token‑based escrow until verification. Pilot with a handful of secondary schools in Lagos and Kogi, charging a modest transaction fee and offering schools a subscription for premium analytics and compliance reporting.
competitor: NELFUND token payment system – government‑backed but does not provide a private SaaS solution with transparent fee breakdowns and escrow for schools.
trend: The rapid rise of blockchain and digital wallet adoption in Africa is making tokenized, transparent payment solutions increasingly viable.

tagline: Unreliable water supply forces street vendors and small shops to halt operations or risk health violations
whyNow: With climate‑driven droughts intensifying across Africa and a recent $487 million African Development Bank package for climate resilience, water shortages are becoming acute for informal businesses now.

marketGap: No digital platform currently offers scheduled, on‑demand water deliveries tailored to the cash‑flow cycles of micro‑enterprises, leaving vendors dependent on unreliable informal suppliers.
executionPlan: Launch an MVP mobile app that aggregates local water tanker operators and lets vendors book deliveries within 24‑hour windows, using a prepaid credit system. Pilot in Lagos and Dakar with 200 vendors, charging a 5% transaction fee and an optional subscription for priority scheduling. Scale by adding IoT tank‑level monitoring and expanding to other West African cities.
competitor: None – existing water delivery services are informal and lack a digital marketplace
trend: Accelerating climate‑induced water scarcity is driving demand for reliable water logistics solutions

title: Co‑Living Match: Affordable Shared Housing Platform

whyNow: Rising rents are outpacing wage growth across Nigeria’s megacities, pushing low‑income households into unsustainable trade‑offs. With urbanisation accelerating, the pressure on housing supply will only intensify, making an affordable co‑living solution urgent now.

marketGap: There is no dedicated digital marketplace that aggregates verified spare rooms or under‑utilised units for low‑income renters, leaving them to rely on informal networks or expensive listings.

trend: Rapid urbanisation and smartphone penetration in Africa are creating a market for tech‑enabled, cost‑saving housing solutions.

title: SolarPay for Small Shops
tagline: Small retailers lose sales every time the grid goes down

executionPlan: Launch a pilot with 20 Abuja shops, installing 5 kW solar‑plus‑battery kits financed through a low‑monthly subscription. executionPlan: Build an API that ingests telecom SIM‑change events and cross‑checks with mobile money provider accounts, triggering instant OTP verification and a temporary hold on transactions. Launch a pilot with one telecom and one mobile money operator, charging a per‑user subscription fee. Scale by licensing the engine to other operators across West Africa.
competitor: None provides an end‑to‑end SIM‑swap protection platform for mobile money.
